The letter X can be challenging for both children and ESL learners alike. It is pronounced in several different ways, and there are not a lot of easy words that contain it in the English language. Here are some X words for kids with pictures to help learners get started.

On this page, you will find flashcards, word lists, and example sentences you can use in the classroom. These X words use the sounds of /ks/, /gz/, and /z/. You will find words that start with X, end with X, and have X in the middle.

Download PDF

You can use these picture cards for activities such as:

Sorting –  This can be done in ways such as alphabetical order, adjectives, verbs, and nouns, color groups, pictures students like and dislike, or any other way that is interesting.

Sentence creation –  Give learners one or more cards and ask them to create a sentence using the words.

Tongue twisters – Mix the cards up and then give students 3 or more cards to make their own silly sentences and tongue twisters.

Matching – Buy cutting the words from the bottom of the pictures you can create a fun picture and word matching activity to help reinforce the vocabulary.

Most of the vocabulary in the above word list is commonly known. However, there are a few words that some people may not be familiar with. These include – 

Flax – This is a plant that is used by people for its fibre, oil, and seeds. It is used to make textiles and food products.

Xerus – This is a kind of squirrel that lives in Africa. They live on the ground in burrows and mostly eat plants and insects.

Xenops – This is a kind of rainforest and jungle bird found in South and Central America. They are very small and behave similarly to woodpeckers.

Practice sentences with X words

Here are some simple sentences for learners to practice X words.

 

He saw a fox and an ox.

Six boxes came from Texas.

Alex says boxing is exciting.

Are there pixies in this galaxy?

There is wax on the textbook.

Exercise is excellent for you.

There’s an axe next to the mailbox.

The onyx xylophone was expensive.

 

Students can also try making their own sentences from the word list. There are also the tongue twisters with X which are quite challenging to read aloud.
